_comment: Spec 115 — the campaign layer's single source. A CAMPAIGN is what we are raising for and who it reaches; it gets a page. A DRIVE is a dated way we raise it; it feeds exactly one campaign and is a row on that campaign's page until it earns its own page (as popcorn did). Adding a drive is appending one object here. Set published:false to keep a verified record on file without publishing it. Dates are ISO (YYYY-MM-DD) and read as LOCAL dates. raised stays null until a number is real.

campaigns.name: Chicago Pickleball: Wheelie Big Dills
campaigns.blurb: One goal for the year ahead: every week first, then the road to the US Open.

parts.label: Every week
parts.detail: A year of court time for 10 to 15 athletes a night, plus memberships for 10, so they can play every week and train to compete. Every new gift starts here.

math.label: Court time
math.calc: a night every week, all year
math.note: A night on court is $225, for 10 to 15 athletes.

math.label: Memberships
math.note: Unlimited sessions, because it takes many sessions a week to compete in tournaments and build a ranking.

parts.label: The Road to the US Open
parts.detail: A season of tournament travel for the crew, ending at the US Open in Naples in spring 2027. The US Open picks players by lottery, so nothing is guaranteed. Money raised earlier for the US Open, the popcorn drive included, keeps its terms and stays on the road.
parts._road: Alec, Nov 11 2026: retire 'send six athletes to the US Open'. The road is the crew's tournaments through the year, ending at the US Open, so the money reaches far more than six athletes. The six named seats are gone. The $21,000 stays, as the road's travel for the year: 21 trips at about $1,000 (Alec, Nov 11 2026: a trip costs 'about 1,000 dollars'). A trip is one athlete at one tournament, so the road counts trips, never seats or a head count. About $3,500 is still what one athlete's US Open has cost (a fact for /numbers and the $3,500 gift), never a seat. Stops: a drive slug is a tournament the crew played (never a claim the fund paid that trip); an object is one still ahead.

stops.line: The first wheelchair division on the APP Tour. Juan asked for it, and five full teams played.
Six medals at The Pickle Lodge: two gold, two silver and two bronze, won by Juan, Bob, Robby, Ken and Amanda.

stops.name: The US Open
stops.line: The last stop, for athletes whose names come up in the lottery.

math.label: Tournament trips
math.note: A trip is one athlete at one tournament: entry fees, travel and an accessible room, at about $1,000. The road's budget is for the stops ahead.

next.label: the Chicago Classic
next.detail: Our goal: free registration, transportation and hotels for every athlete. Gifts past the road go toward it, and it gets its own budget once it has a date.

campaigns._note: One goal, one bar (Alec, Nov 5). Every week ($27,180: a year of nights at ACE, $11,700, plus ten athletes training, $15,480) fills first, then the Road ($21,000). The Classic joins the goal when it has a date and a budget.

drives.name: August popcorn drive
drives.supports: The August popcorn drive raised money for the US Open campaign that grew into The Road to the US Open. That money keeps its terms and stays on the road.
drives._supports_original: The appeal as it ran in August 2026 (kept for the record, never published again): The August popcorn drive supports Send 6 to the US Open Spring 2027: equipment, training, and travel for six adaptive pickleball athletes.
drives.summary: Double Good handles orders and shipping. The fund receives 50% of popcorn sales toward the campaign.
drives._supporters: Double Good's count of people who bought from the store (Alec, Nov 7 2026: 'at least 80 something from our popcorn fundraiser'). Givebutter's donor count (online gifts) never included them; /numbers shows both, apart, so no one is counted twice.

drives._note: Spec 115 D1 resolved 2026-07-25: ATL has athletes in this bracket, so it is published. It carries NO campaign field on purpose. We only compete here; APP hosts it and Shriners Children's benefits, so it raises nothing for us and must never appear under a campaign's 'what is feeding this'. It is on the calendar because our athletes are there.
drives.name: APP Vlasic Classic Chicago
drives.summary: Our athletes play the Wheelchair Open Doubles bracket on Sunday the 9th. Free to watch, and the best look you will get at what the fund pays for.

drives._note: A tournament our athletes play in. The Pickle Lodge hosts it and it raises nothing for us, so it has no campaign field and QR campaign-follow ignores it. Dates, venue and address from the official listing (pickleballtournaments.com/tournaments/monster-smash-2026, read 2026-10-02). Eastern time.
